tasks.title: Leak-free cache
tasks.statement: Write ObjectCache on top of WeakValueDictionary: the method get(key, factory) returns the cached object, and if there is none (or it has already died), creates one via factory() and remembers it; __len__ is the number of live entries. The cache must not extend the life of objects.
tasks.hint: self._data = weakref.WeakValueDictionary(); get: obj = self._data.get(key); if None, create it and store it.

tasks.title: Weak reference with a callback
tasks.statement: Write watch(obj, callback): it returns a weak reference to obj which, when the object dies, calls callback(type_name), where type_name is type(obj).__name__, remembered in advance.
tasks.hint: name = type(obj).__name__; return weakref.ref(obj, lambda _ref: callback(name)).

tasks.title: finalize instead of __del__
tasks.statement: Write track(name, log): it creates and returns a Handle object, and via weakref.finalize registers the record «закрыт <name>» to be appended to the list log when the object dies. The Handle class has no __del__.
tasks.hint: h = Handle(); weakref.finalize(h, log.append, f"закрыт {name}"); return h.

tasks.title: A cycle and the garbage collector
tasks.statement: Write cycle_demo(): disable the collector (gc.disable()), create two Node objects that refer to each other, take a weak reference to the first one and delete both names; return the tuple (alive_before_collection, alive_after_collection), where "after" means after gc.collect(). At the end, turn the collector back on.
tasks.hint: a.other = b; b.other = a; ref = weakref.ref(a); del a, b; before = ref() is not None; gc.collect(); after = ref() is not None; in finally: gc.enable().

tasks.title: Your own __deepcopy__
tasks.statement: A Document has a text, a cache (dict), and a list of child documents. Write __deepcopy__(self, memo): the text and the child documents are copied deeply (pass memo), and the cache in the copy must be a new empty dict.
tasks.hint: new = type(self)(self.text, copy.deepcopy(self.children, memo)); return new (the cache is created empty in __init__). Don't forget import copy.

tasks.title: Peak memory via tracemalloc
tasks.statement: Write peak_bytes(func): start tracemalloc, call func(), return the peak number of allocated bytes (get_traced_memory()[1]), and stop tracemalloc.
tasks.hint: tracemalloc.start(); func(); peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()[1]; tracemalloc.stop(); return peak.

tasks.title: Sum of squares without a list
tasks.statement: The function sum_squares(n) computes the sum of squares of 0..n-1, but builds a whole list for it. Rewrite it so that no extra data piles up in memory (a generator expression); the result must not change.
tasks.hint: return sum(i * i for i in range(n)).

tasks.title: Bound the cache
tasks.statement: slow_square caches results without a limit (maxsize=None), so memory grows forever. Limit the cache to 128 entries so that the most recent calls still hit the cache.

tasks.title: A slice without copying
tasks.statement: Write middle(data, start, stop): return the buffer slice data[start:stop] as a memoryview (without copying), so that changes to the original bytearray are visible through the slice, and writing through the slice changes the original buffer.
